_comment: Read at compile time, so the config can never silently drift: Rust reads it in `src-tauri/build.rs` (which re-emits environment variables for `src-tauri/src/lib.rs` to read via `env!`), and `src/main.tsx` imports the background-service pair and the launcher base URL. Change the values here and rebuild.
_local_granted_scopes_comment: The host's granted scopes: gatekeeper seeds the `wildflower-host` client's allowed_scopes and mints the host owner token from this. MUST cover gatekeeper-rust's WILDFLOWER_WIDEST_SCOPES (`system/*.cruds` + `wildflower/*.cruds`) or the launcher loses `/access/*` — gatekeeper asserts this at boot. `wildflower/launch` is an owner *capability* (not part of WIDEST): a *known* scope not covered by the `wildflower/*` wildcard, so the app-launch surface would 403 the owner without it listed explicitly.
_first_party_client_id_comment: The `client_id` of the host's first-party OAuth client. gatekeeper-rust seeds the client row and mints the host owner token under this id; the `FIRST_PARTY_CLIENT_ID` consts in gatekeeper-rust/gatekeeper-core are the standalone/test fallback only.
_launcher_base_url_comment: The hosted launcher (`apps/launcher/launcher-web`'s `main-web` build) the host links browsers to — see `shared_structures_rust::launcher`. Release builds use `launcher_base_url` (held to branding-core's `sectionUrl('launcher')` by `apps/launcher/launcher-web/src/launcher-address.test.ts`); debug builds use the `main-web` dev server on `slices/apps/dev-app-ports.json`'s `launcher-dev` port, which `src-tauri/build.rs` reads. `launcher_base_url` is also the launcher a new server gets, in every build: the host gives it to each server it adds (Rust, re-emitted by `src-tauri/build.rs`), and the base's server page offers Reset to default while a server's launcher differs from it (TS, imported by `src/main.tsx`).
_background_service_comment: How the background service starts the Wildflower server: the text of Android's persistent foreground-service notification, and its Android foreground-service type. The host starts the service with these (Rust, re-emitted by `src-tauri/build.rs`), and the Tauri entry hands the same pair to the plugin's `configureRecovery` for the restarts the plugin makes itself (TS, imported by `src/main.tsx`). The type must also be in `tauri.conf.json`'s `androidForegroundServiceTypes` and be the one the Android manifest narrows the plugin's service to; host tests hold both to this value.
